intent_signal: Transactional-commercial with strong research overlay. Most ranking pages are camp homepages/booking pages (transactional), but the top informational result is a beginner-comparison listicle — searchers are comparison-shopping a destination camp, weighing cost, beginner-friendliness, location (Phuket vs Chiang Mai vs Bangkok) and stay/train logistics before booking.
common_ground: Phuket and Bangkok dominate; Chiang Mai under-represented

gap.description: Nobody on the SERP owns the warm, family-run, woman-led, open-air Chiang Mai positioning combined with transparent up-front pricing and a real DTV long-stay visa pathway. The Phuket/Bangkok leaders are explicitly elite or boot-camp ('Built for Training, Not for Comfort', '#1', UFC-champion endorsements, fight-camp immersion) — the opposite of Wildcat's familial, non-hardcore, golden-hour garden vibe. Chiang Mai is represented only by The Camp (boot-camp framing, no named coaches, no posted prices) and scattered listicle mentions (Lanna, Santai). DTV visa is mentioned by exactly one ranking page (The Camp) and never explained; transparent published per-week/per-month THB pricing on the landing page is essentially absent across all top results. A page that fuses 'come for the fight, stay for the family' warmth + Chiang Mai open-air + named owner (Meaw) + honest THB pricing + DTV long-stay support directly answers the PAA cluster (cost, beginners-welcome, which camp, visa, Chiang Mai vs Phuket) that the current results only partially serve.

weakness: Pricing covered superficially — leaders push you to a separate page or hide rates entirely; the head-term SERP has no transparent THB pricing answer despite cost being the #1 PAA
DTV / long-stay visa touched by only one camp (The Camp) and never actually explained
Chiang Mai under-served — head term is Phuket-dominated; Chiang Mai is a thin slice (one boot-camp homepage + listicle mentions)
Beginner reassurance lives mostly in third-party listicles, not on the camps' own ranking pages — camps default to elite/champion framing
Family / non-hardcore / woman-run identity is entirely absent from page-1 camps (all are elite, fight-camp, or 'built for training not comfort')
Open-air / garden / golden-hour atmosphere is claimed by none of the top results
recommended_angle: Re-cast /stay-train as the warm, family-run, open-air Chiang Mai alternative to the elite Phuket/Bangkok fight camps — own 'come for the fight, stay for the family' with transparent THB pricing, beginners-genuinely-welcome reassurance, and a real DTV long-stay visa pathway, directly answering the cost / beginner / which-camp / visa / Chiang Mai-vs-Phuket PAA cluster nobody on page 1 fully serves.
